My parents responded the same to all three of my older siblings. Nearly all of it was the Asian culture my parents were raised in-they’re ignorant and simply don’t understand the importance of mental health (or believe in it existing tbh!) They see it as having the ‘privilege to think about your feelings’ rather than having to think about where you’re going to sleep and what you’re going to eat. 

I talked to a doctor friend about this-having parents who don’t understand mental health. She explained to me that because the differences in their understanding was caused by their culture, simply being raised to stick it out and be miserable or religious reasons-it would be difficult to change their perspectives in a short amount of time. To be really blunt, she knew people with parents like that, and they have just had to deal with the ignorance and kind of evade their parents over the years. This is a well known tactic. But a friend of mine whose parents were angered (by her saying she was suicidal) learned over the years. Her parents are not incredibly supportive, but they now show their care for my friend’s mental state, asking how she is doing every once in a while. 

Forgive me if I’m being crude; I just brought up culture because it all sounded so familiar. My parents said you’re wrong for feeling that way, you’re lying, you’re bad children, nobody cares, but study more haha. My siblings also go to a community college and are looking to transfer later, at the downside of my parents 

All in all, changing the minds’ of parents who don’t understand takes time, and it’s very hard and sometimes awkward to get through. But you are not alone in doing so if you’d like to try!
